Luis —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below and I attached a short matrix (privdeploy-pricing-matrix.xlsx) and a one-pager (northbridge-platform-fee-options.pdf). Quick summary:

- Platform fee vs site/operator licensing: platform fee is a centralized monthly entitlement that covers control-plane, observability retention (configurable), and higher-level SLAs. Operator licenses (per-site) are what run the inference runtime on customer hardware (per-GPU or per-node depending on architecture). For multi-site setups you can choose:
  Option A — site licenses for each location + reduced platform fee (good if you fully own infra at each site).
  Option B — operator license anchor in primary site + lightweight site licenses for DR/edge (recommended for NorthBridge given mixed cloud footprints).

- Pilot amortization / conditional discount: we can offer a pilot credit structure (example included in matrix): 3-month pilot = 100% credit on platform fee up to $90k; if you convert to a 12-month committed agreement within 30 days of pilot end, we convert that credit to an ongoing 15% discount on platform fee for first 12 months. If you do a 6-month commit instead, conversion discount is 8%. This is conditional on minimum committed usage (we modeled ~200 inference units/month in the sheet).

- Support tiers / SLAs:
  - Standard: business hours support, P1 target 8hr response, no SRE retainer.
  - Premium: 24x7 on-call, P1 target 1hr response, includes optional SRE retainer (monthly) for runbook ops and on-call bridging.
  - Enterprise SRE: Dedicated SRE retainer, guaranteed runbook onboarding and quarterly incident reviews, with higher observability retention.

Action items:
1) Take a look at the matrix and pick which option you want priced out (A vs B + tier).
2) Tell us expected pilot start date and expected GPU/node counts per site — we used placeholder numbers in the attachment.

Marissa and Karthik are looped in to confirm technical assumptions and finalize the numbers.

Thanks —
Aisha
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Hi Luis —

Following up with a technical note to explain Option B (anchor + lightweight sites). Key points to share with your engineering team:

- Anchor site runs full operator licenses (KV cache optimized) and serves as primary model store. Lightweight sites can be configured with a smaller node pool (quantized models, limited local cache) and are compatible with automated fallback to anchor in the event of heavy load.
- Cross-site failover adds nominal network egress (we show a conservative estimate in the matrix).
- The pilot credit above applies only to the platform fee and observability retention — operator licenses are discounted on commit but are not fully creditable (we reserve a 30% non-creditable setup margin to cover packaging & operator licensing administrative costs).

I also added a recommended support mapping for you: Premium tier for production pilot, then evaluate Enterprise SRE at conversion if you expect tighter incident windows.

If helpful I can produce a short SOW snippet (one page) that ties the pilot credit to conversion milestones; that speeds procurement review.

-M
